# FastMCP Docs

Swagger-style documentation generator for FastMCP servers. Automatically creates beautiful, interactive API documentation from your FastMCP tools.

## Features

- 🎨 **Swagger-Style UI** - Clean, modern interface similar to Swagger UI
- 🔍 **Search Functionality** - Quickly find tools by name, description, or tags
- 🏷️ **Tag-Based Organization** - Tools grouped by tags for easy navigation
- 📝 **Auto-Generated** - Extracts documentation from your FastMCP tools automatically
- ⚙️ **Highly Configurable** - Customize title, description, links, and more
- 🚀 **Easy Integration** - Simple 3-line setup
- 📚 **OpenAPI Compatible** - Generates OpenAPI 3.1.0 schema
- 🔄 **Version Support** - Compatible with both FastMCP v2 and v3

## Installation

```bash
pip install fastmcp-docs
```

## Quick Start

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp_docs import FastMCPDocs
import asyncio

# Create your FastMCP server
mcp = FastMCP("My MCP Server")

# Register your tools
@mcp.tool(tags=["example"])
def hello_world(name: str = "World"):
    """Say hello to someone"""
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

# Setup documentation (3 lines!)
docs = FastMCPDocs(mcp, title="My MCP Tools")
asyncio.run(docs.setup())

# Run server
mcp.run()
```

That's it! Your documentation is now available at:
- **UI**: http://localhost:8000/docs
- **OpenAPI**: http://localhost:8000/openapi.json
- **Tools API**: http://localhost:8000/api/tools

## Configuration

### Basic Configuration

```python
from fastmcp_docs import FastMCPDocs

docs = FastMCPDocs(
    mcp=mcp,
    title="My MCP Tools",
    version="1.0.0",
    description="API documentation for my awesome MCP server",
    base_url="https://api.example.com",
)
```

### Adding Documentation Links

```python
docs = FastMCPDocs(
    mcp=mcp,
    title="My MCP Tools",
    docs_links=[
        {"text": "GitHub Repository", "url": "https://github.com/..."},
        {"text": "User Guide", "url": "https://docs.example.com"},
        {"text": "API Reference", "url": "https://api.example.com/reference"}
    ]
)
```

### Customizing the Favicon

```python
# Use default favicon (green circle with M)
docs = FastMCPDocs(mcp, title="My Tools")

# Use custom favicon URL
docs = FastMCPDocs(
    mcp,
    title="My Tools",
    favicon_url="https://example.com/my-icon.ico"
)

# Use local favicon file
docs = FastMCPDocs(
    mcp,
    title="My Tools",
    favicon_url="/static/favicon.png"
)
```

### Advanced Configuration

```python
from fastmcp_docs import FastMCPDocs, FastMCPDocsConfig, DocsLink

# Create custom configuration
config = FastMCPDocsConfig(
    title="My MCP Tools",
    version="2.0.0",
    description="Advanced API documentation",
    base_url="https://api.example.com",
    docs_links=[
        DocsLink(text="GitHub", url="https://github.com/..."),
        DocsLink(text="Docs", url="https://docs.example.com")
    ],
    page_title_emoji="🤖",
    favicon_url="https://example.com/favicon.ico",

    # Customize route paths
    api_tools_route="/api/tools",
    openapi_route="/openapi.json",
    docs_ui_route="/docs",

    # OpenAPI settings
    openapi_version="3.1.0",
    openapi_servers=[
        {"url": "https://api.example.com", "description": "Production"},
        {"url": "https://staging.example.com", "description": "Staging"}
    ],

    # Options
    enable_cors=True,
    verbose=True
)

# Use custom config
docs = FastMCPDocs(mcp, config=config)
```

## Adding Descriptions to Tool Parameters

To get parameter descriptions in the documentation, use type Annotated:

```python
from typing import Annotated

@mcp.tool(tags=["greetings"])
def greet(
    name: Annotated[str, "Name of the person to greet"],
    greeting: Annotated[str, "Greeting to use"] = "Hello"
) -> str:
    """Greet someone with a custom message"""
    return f"{greeting}, {name}!"
```

## Complete Example

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp_docs import FastMCPDocs
from typing import Annotated
import asyncio

# Create server
mcp = FastMCP("My MCP Server")


@mcp.tool(tags=["deployment"], annotations={"title": "Deploy Application"})
def deploy(
    environment: Annotated[str, "Target environment (dev, staging, prod)"],
    version: Annotated[str, "Version to deploy"],
    dry_run: Annotated[bool = "Perform dry run without actual deployment"] = False
) -> str:
    """Deploy application to specified environment

    This tool deploys the application to the target environment
    with the specified version. Use dry_run to test without deploying.
    """
    if dry_run:
        return f"DRY RUN: Would deploy v{version} to {environment}"
    return f"Deployed v{version} to {environment}"

# Setup documentation
docs = FastMCPDocs(
    mcp=mcp,
    title="My FastMCP Tools",
    version="1.0.0",
    description="This is my FastMCP Tools Documention",
    base_url="https://mcp.example.com",
    page_title_emoji="🛠️",
    docs_links=[
        {"text": "Tools Guide", "url": "https://docs.example.com/tools-guide"}
    ]
)

# Run setup
asyncio.run(docs.setup())

# Start server
if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run(transport="sse", host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)
```

## API Routes

FastMCP Docs automatically creates the following routes:

| Route | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `/docs` | Interactive Swagger-style UI |
| `/openapi.json` | OpenAPI 3.1.0 schema |
| `/api/tools` | List all tools with metadata |
| `/api/tools/{tool_name}` | Get specific tool details |

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

FastMCP Docs is a Python library that generates Swagger-style documentation for FastMCP servers. It automatically extracts tool information from FastMCP instances and provides a web-based UI similar to Swagger/OpenAPI documentation interfaces.

## Key Commands

### Development Setup
```bash
# Create and activate virtual environment
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate

# Install package in development mode
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

### Testing
```bash
# Run all tests
pytest

# Run with verbose output
pytest -v

# Run specific test file
pytest tests/test_extractor.py
```

### Code Formatting
```bash
# Format all code
black fastmcp_docs/
```

### Type Checking
```bash
# Type check with mypy
mypy fastmcp_docs/
```

### Building and Distribution
```bash
# Clean previous builds
rm -rf dist/ fastmcp_docs.egg-info/

# Build package
uv run python -m build

# Check distribution
uv run python -m twine check dist/*

# Upload to PyPI
uv run python -m twine upload dist/*

# Install from local build
pip install -e .
```

**Version Bump Process:**
1. Update version in `pyproject.toml`
2. Run full build and distribution process above
3. Commit and tag the release:
   ```bash
   git add -A
   git commit -m "Release v1.0.0: Add FastMCP v3 support"
   git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "Version 1.0.0"
   git push && git push --tags
   ```

### Running Examples
```bash
# Run basic usage example
python examples/basic_usage.py
```

## Architecture

### Core Components

The library consists of five main modules:

1. **`__init__.py`** - Main entry point exposing the `FastMCPDocs` class
   - Provides the public API for library users
   - Coordinates between extractor, routes, and config modules
   - Setup is async because it needs to call async methods on FastMCP server

2. **`config.py`** - Configuration dataclasses
   - `FastMCPDocsConfig`: Main configuration with route paths, OpenAPI settings, UI customization
   - `DocsLink`: Simple dataclass for documentation links
   - Configuration supports dict-to-DocsLink conversion in `__post_init__`

3. **`extractor.py`** - Tool documentation extraction
   - `ToolExtractor` class extracts metadata from FastMCP tools
   - Retrieves tool descriptions, parameters, tags, and input schemas
   - Falls back to function signature inspection if schemas not available
   - Converts Python type annotations to JSON schema types

4. **`routes.py`** - HTTP route registration
   - `RouteRegistrar` class registers endpoints with FastMCP server
   - Creates four main routes: `/api/tools`, `/api/tools/{tool_name}`, `/openapi.json`, `/docs`
   - Handles CORS headers when enabled
   - Generates OpenAPI 3.1.0 schema from tools registry

5. **`templates.py`** - HTML and SVG templates
   - Contains the Swagger-style UI HTML template
   - Includes default favicon SVG generator
   - Templates are embedded as strings for zero external dependencies

### Data Flow

1. User creates FastMCP server and registers tools using `@mcp.tool()` decorator
2. User creates `FastMCPDocs` instance, passing the MCP server
3. User calls `await docs.setup()` (must be async)
4. Setup process:
   - `ToolExtractor` queries MCP server for all registered tools
   - For each tool, extracts name, description, parameters, tags, and schemas
   - `RouteRegistrar` registers custom routes with the MCP server's Starlette app
   - Routes serve the tools registry as JSON/HTML
5. When server runs, documentation endpoints are available

### Important Patterns

- **Async Setup Required**: `docs.setup()` must be called with `asyncio.run()` before `mcp.run()` because FastMCP's tool introspection is async
- **Type Annotation Support**: Uses `typing.Annotated` to extract parameter descriptions (e.g., `Annotated[str, "description"]`)
- **Tag-Based Organization**: Tools can have multiple tags for categorization in the UI
- **Custom Routes**: Uses FastMCP's `@mcp.custom_route()` decorator to register documentation endpoints
- **Zero Dependencies**: No template engine needed - HTML/SVG embedded as strings

### Configuration Options

The library supports both direct parameter passing and config object:
- Direct: `FastMCPDocs(mcp, title="...", version="...")`
- Config object: `FastMCPDocs(mcp, config=FastMCPDocsConfig(...))`

Key configuration areas:
- Basic info (title, version, description, base_url)
- Route paths (customizable endpoints)
- OpenAPI settings (version, servers)
- UI customization (emoji, favicon, docs links)
- Options (CORS, verbose logging)

## Development Notes

- Python 3.10+ required
- Dependencies: `fastmcp>=2.0.0`, `starlette>=0.27.0`
- Package structure follows setuptools with `pyproject.toml`
- Version defined in `pyproject.toml` (currently 0.2.2)
- MIT licensed

## FastMCP Version Compatibility

The library supports both fastmcp v2 and v3:

**v2 API (fastmcp 2.x)**:
- Uses `get_tools()` which returns `dict[str, Tool]`
- Tools accessed directly from dictionary

**v3 API (fastmcp 3.x)**:
- Uses `list_tools()` which returns `list[Tool]`
- Breaking change: method renamed and return type changed from dict to list
- The extractor automatically detects the available method and adapts

The extractor handles both versions automatically by:
1. Checking if `list_tools()` exists (v3)
2. Falling back to `get_tools()` if not found (v2)
3. Converting list to dict internally for uniform processing

---

# FastMCP v3 Support

Source: https://github.com/orco82/fastmcp-docs/blob/main/FASTMCP_V3_SUPPORT.md

# FastMCP v3 Support

This document describes the changes made to support both FastMCP v2 and v3.

## Breaking Changes in FastMCP v3

FastMCP v3 introduced several breaking changes:

### Tool Listing API Change

**v2**: `get_tools()` → returns `dict[str, Tool]`
```python
tools = await server.get_tools()
tool = tools["my_tool"]  # Dict access by name
```

**v3**: `list_tools()` → returns `list[Tool]`
```python
tools = await server.list_tools()
tool = next((t for t in tools if t.name == "my_tool"), None)  # List iteration
```

## Implementation

The `fastmcp-docs` library now supports both versions automatically through runtime detection in `extractor.py`:

```python
async def extract_tools(self, mcp) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        # Try v3 API first (list_tools returns list)
        if hasattr(mcp, 'list_tools'):
            tools = await mcp.list_tools()
            # Convert list to dict for uniform processing
            tools_dict = {tool.name: tool for tool in tools}
            if self.verbose:
                print(f"\nFound {len(tools_dict)} tools to document (fastmcp v3)")
        # Fall back to v2 API (get_tools returns dict)
        elif hasattr(mcp, 'get_tools'):
            tools_dict = await mcp.get_tools()
            if self.verbose:
                print(f"\nFound {len(tools_dict)} tools to document (fastmcp v2)")
        else:
            raise AttributeError("MCP server has neither list_tools() nor get_tools() methods")
    except Exception as e:
        # Handle errors...
```

## Version Detection Strategy

1. Check if `list_tools()` method exists (v3 API)
2. If not, fall back to `get_tools()` (v2 API)
3. Convert list to dict internally for uniform processing
4. Rest of the code works the same regardless of version

## Benefits

- **No Breaking Changes**: Users don't need to update their code
- **Automatic Detection**: Library automatically detects which version is installed
- **Backward Compatible**: Works with v2 (2.x) installations
- **Forward Compatible**: Works with v3 (3.x) installations
- **Verbose Logging**: Shows which API version is being used when verbose=True

## Testing

Test with FastMCP v2:
```bash
pip install "fastmcp>=2.0.0,<3.0.0"
python examples/basic_usage.py
# Should print: "Found X tools to document (fastmcp v2)"
```

Test with FastMCP v3:
```bash
pip install "fastmcp>=3.0.0"
python examples/basic_usage.py
# Should print: "Found X tools to document (fastmcp v3)"
```

## Dependencies

Updated `pyproject.toml`:
```toml
dependencies = [
    "fastmcp>=2.0.0",  # Changed from >=0.1.0 to support both v2 and v3
    "starlette>=0.27.0",
]
```

The minimum version is now 2.0.0 (not 0.1.0) to ensure proper API stability.
